- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

content.text: I have what I need. Let me confirm the two service-level triggers.

h14.

**Computation site.** The derived metadata lives on `Memo.Payload.Property` (proto `storepb.MemoPayload_Property`). It is (re)built by `RebuildMemoPayload` in `server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:74`, which delegates to the markdown service's single-pass `ExtractAll` (`internal/markdown/markdown.go:356`, the AST walk at lines 383–408). `ExtractAll` sets both `Payload.Tags` and `Payload.Property`; the standalone property extractor is `ExtractProperties` at `internal/markdown/markdown.go:193`.

**Triggers (what causes recomputation).**
- Memo creation — `CreateMemo` calls `RebuildMemoPayload` on the new memo (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:108`).
- Memo update whose content changed — `UpdateMemo` reassigns `memo.Content` then calls `RebuildMemoPayload` (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:447`).
- Bulk backfill — the `memopayload.Runner.RunOnce` batch job rebuilds the payload of every memo (`server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:27`, calling `RebuildMemoPayload` at line 52 and persisting via `UpdateMemo`).

**Extracted properties** (parsed from the memo's markdown content, `internal/markdown/markdown.go:383–408`):
- `Title` — text of the first block-level child of the document if it is an H1 heading (`extractHeadingText`, line 387).
- `HasLink` — true if any link node is present (`gast.KindLink`, line 394).
- `HasCode` — true for any code block/fenced code block/inline code span (line 397).
- `HasTaskList` — true if any task checkbox exists (line 400).
- `HasIncompleteTasks` — true if any task checkbox is unchecked (lines 401–404).

(`ExtractAll` also populates `Payload.Tags` from `#tag` nodes in the same pass, `internal/markdown/markdown.go:376–377`.)

These derived fields feed lists/previews and stats — e.g. `convertMemoPropertyFromStore` (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go:49`) and the user stats aggregation (`server/router/api/v1/user_service_stats.go:141–151`).

## Summary

The memos project (Go backend) derives memo metadata in two ways: **persisted payload fields** (Tags + Property) computed at write time, and a **snippet** computed on the fly at read/convert time.

### 1. WHERE the derived metadata is computed

**Core computation — `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go`** (goldmark AST-based markdown service):

- **`ExtractAll`** (lines 356-422) — the primary single-pass extractor. Walks the parsed markdown AST and populates an `ExtractedData` struct (`Tags`, `Mentions`, `Property`).
- **`ExtractProperties`** (lines 193-241) — standalone variant that computes just the boolean `Property` struct.
- **`GenerateSnippet`** (lines 264-346) — builds the plain-text preview/summary.
- Helpers: `extractHeadingText` (lines 173-179) pulls the title text from an H1; `truncateAtWord` (lines 472-489) truncates the snippet at a word boundary with " ..." suffix.

**Payload assembly — `/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go`**:
- **`RebuildMemoPayload`** (lines 74-88) calls `markdownService.ExtractAll(...)` and assigns results into `memo.Payload.Tags` and `memo.Payload.Property` (lines 85-86).

**Snippet wrapper — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go`**:
- **`getMemoContentSnippet`** (lines 83-90) calls `GenerateSnippet([]byte(content), 64)` — note the fixed max length of **64** characters.

### 2. WHICH operations trigger recomputation

**Persisted Property + Tags** (via `RebuildMemoPayload`):
- **On create** — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:108` (in `CreateMemo`).
- **On update, only when content changes** — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:435-451`. It is guarded by `if path == "content"` in the `UpdateMask` loop (line 436); `RebuildMemoPayload` runs at line 447 and the new payload is written via `update.Payload = memo.Payload` (line 451).
- **Bulk backfill/migration** — `/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:27-72` (`RunOnce`) rebuilds the payload for all existing memos in batches of 100 and persists each via `Store.UpdateMemo`.

**Snippet** — computed at **read/response-conversion time**, not persisted:
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go:76-80` in the main memo→proto converter (runs on every memo returned by the API).
- Also for relations (`memo_service_converter.go:225, 248`; `memo_relation_service.go:154, 162`) and notifications (`user_service_notifications.go:323`).

### 3. WHAT the computation extracts

**`Property`** (`storepb.MemoPayload_Property`) — derived in `ExtractAll` / `ExtractProperties` (markdown.go lines 383-408):
- **`Title`** — plain text of the first block-level node if it's an H1 heading (lines 384-388).
- **`HasLink`** — true if any link node exists (`gast.KindLink`, line 393).
- **`HasCode`** — true for any code block, fenced code block, or inline code span (line 396).
- **`HasTaskList`** — true if any task checkbox exists (line 400).
- **`HasIncompleteTasks`** — true if any task checkbox is unchecked (lines 401-404).

**`Tags`** — deduplicated `#tag` names (case preserved), excluding tags inside links/images (lines 376-378, plus `asMemoTagNode`/`uniquePreserveCase`). `Mentions` (@username, lowercased) are also extracted but consumed elsewhere, not stored in the payload by `RebuildMemoPayload`.

**`Snippet`** — plain-text preview from `GenerateSnippet` (lines 264-346): walks the AST concatenating text, skips fenced/indented code blocks (keeps inline code), inserts spaces between block elements, renders `#tags` and autolink URLs, then truncates at a word boundary to a max of **64** characters.

**Response mapping** (`memo_service_converter.go:47-51, 76-80`): `memo.Payload.Tags` → `Memo.Tags`, `memo.Payload.Property` → `Memo.Property` (via `convertMemoPropertyFromStore`, lines 315-325), and the freshly computed `snippet` → `Memo.Snippet`.</result>
